title: [D9 Governance] Decision records, deferred register and open-question closure
summary: The governance knowledge that was only in reports and code comments is now in the repository as registers that a test keeps true. `docs/decisions/README.md` maps every blocking question in `concept/08-open-questions.md` to the record that settled it (one row says STILL OPEN, and it is); five new records settle the enrichment and analyst questions that had no record — 0041 enrichment status, 0042 port qualification, 0043 the compromised flag, 0044 the snapshot scheme, 0045 who decides the analyst is unsure — and 0046 records where a failed or inconclusive result lives. `docs/deferred.md` is thirteen deferred capabilities, each with a falsifiable re-entry test and what exists instead; `docs/hazards.md` is `concept/08`'s ten accepted risks, each with what is actually done about it; `docs/sources/` is five source records, each opening by stating whether it was written from a fetched artifact — and two of the five say NOT, because they were not.
assumption_validated: That the blocking open questions really were settled inside the stage that needed them, rather than being carried as open. Result: eleven of the twelve were, and writing the closure map is what proved it — six already had a record (0018, 0019, 0022, 0023, 0025, 0026), five were settled in the migrations and the policy package with no findable record and now have one, and exactly one is genuinely still open (the silently lost record at a catch-up boundary, which is why `concept/01` puts 'identical inputs replay identically' on the not-claimable list). A negative result worth carrying: the registers are copies of the concept notes, so the assumption that mattered was that a copy can be kept honest by execution rather than by discipline — `tests/test_governance.py` parses both notes on every run and fails on drift in either direction.
makes_buildable: A later session can tell settled from open without reading forty records: the closure map names the record per question, `docs/deferred.md` names the two-part re-entry test per deferred capability (so a task proposing one has a bar to clear rather than a diagram to point at), and `docs/sources/` is the template a sixth source record has to fill — provenance line first. `docs/deferred.md` §13 is the concrete next dependency: it states both halves the second live provider needs, one of which (an engine-side daily ledger) is a design constraint on any future cross-run budget.

verification.detail: 2137 passed in 895.44s (0:14:55), run in one workspace with nothing else running. tests/test_governance.py contributes 242 tests: the hazard table and the deferral list are parsed out of concept/08 and concept/01 on every run and compared in BOTH directions, every record's number is checked contiguous and unreused, the index is checked against the directory both ways, every registered source in helena.enrichment.SOURCES is checked to have a record, every record is checked to open with its provenance line, and every prds/reports/task-*.json is checked to carry the three fields that hold a negative result (all 55 do). A DELIBERATELY vacuous test is documented as such: no module is labelled `Maturity: deferred` today, so the parametrized register check over the package cannot fail — test_the_register_check_rejects_a_deferred_module_with_no_key calls the same function on a synthetic docstring and requires it to fail, and test_no_module_is_labelled_deferred_yet_and_that_is_the_current_fact records the fact as an assertion rather than as a memory. An EARLIER full-suite run had one failure, tests/test_durability.py::test_the_restored_schema_holds_the_rows_the_backup_came_from — `['helena_signal_host_context'] did not come back, and none of them reads the clock`. It did not reproduce: that module passed 26/26 alone, and the clean full-suite run above is green. See failed_approaches for what I did that probably caused it.

invariant_conflicts.kind: task step vs the no-duplicate-home rule
invariant_conflicts.detail: The task asks for `docs/decisions/` with 'a short record per settled question' naming eleven questions. Six of the eleven ALREADY had a record — TLS parameter selection is 0018 §3, rendering bounds 0019, per-source thresholds 0023 §4 plus config/policy.toml, budget values and retry count 0026 and 0020 §5, negative caching 0025 §3, cache-key normalization 0025 §2. Writing a second record for each would create two homes for one decision, which is the thing `sql/migrations/0011` and `0002_aggregation_version.sql` argue against by name: two copies that can drift are worse than none. Resolved by writing records only for the five questions with no record and making the eleventh (who decides the analyst is unsure) 0045, then building the closure map in docs/decisions/README.md so every one of the eleven is findable from its question. Nothing was left uncovered; six rows point at existing records rather than new ones.

`concept/08-open-questions.md` still presented every blocking question as open, while the answers had existed in the code since roughly task 27. `concept/instruction.md` §4 forbids papering that over, so concept/08 now carries a dated note at the head of the blocking section saying the questions are answered and pointing at the map — and the questions themselves are left exactly as written, because a question rewritten into its answer loses what was not known when the work started. Same shape for concept/01's deferred list and concept/08's hazard table: a pointer to the register, not a rewrite. These are the only edits to `concept/` in this task and none of them changes a claim.

deferred: A record for `docs/evaluation-corpus.md`, which task 54 explicitly handed to this task to decide. Decided: no ADR. Its reasoning is already in the document, `docs/acceptance.md` set the precedent of an artifact without one, and a record that only pointed at a document would be the second home this task spent its first invariant_conflict avoiding. The document is instead cited from docs/deferred.md §7 and docs/hazards.md §1 and §6, which is what it was missing.

Resolving the wording discrepancy task 54 flagged in `docs/decisions/0028` §7 — 'the publisher expires IOCs older than six months', which reads as first-seen and is not what the export shows (633 ip:port entries first seen more than 183 days before the snapshot are in it, all with activity inside its two-day window). Deliberately not touched. The sentence is right if 'older' means 'last seen', and settling which the publisher means needs a probe of the live API against a known-expired indicator — an external fact, not a wording choice, and guessing it is exactly what this project has been burned by. `docs/sources/threatfox.md` records the expiry behaviour as measured (an expired IOC is absent from both surfaces) without repeating the ambiguous clause.

A link checker over the markdown. Every relative link written here was hand-checked and the two that matter are tested (`test_the_index_names_no_record_that_does_not_exist` and `test_every_record_is_in_the_index`), but nothing walks the whole of `docs/` resolving hrefs. It would be a real test; it is a different task's worth of scope and would want to cover the ~50 pre-existing documents too.

Diagnosing the durability drill's intermittent failure. It is task 53's test, it did not reproduce, and a guess at the cause committed as a fix would be worse than the note in failed_approaches. The lead is there for whoever sees it again.
lessons: THE BLOCKING OPEN QUESTIONS IN `concept/08` ARE CLOSED, AND THE MAP IS `docs/decisions/README.md`. Do not read concept/08's blocking section as a to-do list — it is preserved as written, with a note at its head. Exactly one row of the map says STILL OPEN: the record silently lost at a catch-up boundary. That one is why replayability is a goal and not a claim, and why `concept/01` lists 'identical inputs replay identically' as not claimable.

SIX OF THE ELEVEN 'SETTLED QUESTIONS' A TASK ASKS YOU TO RECORD MAY ALREADY HAVE A RECORD. Check before writing one: this project treats two homes for one decision as worse than none, and the existing forty records are dense enough that the answer is usually inside one of them under a different heading. `grep -ril` over `docs/decisions/` for the question's own words found every one of the six.

`in_flight` IS NOT AN ENRICHMENT STATUS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. There are six states a reader must tell apart and four names: the sixth — claims written, ledger row not — has not finished having an outcome, and what makes it safe is an ORDERING (the ledger row is the commit point) rather than a fifth status value. `in_flight` exists one layer up as an agent-contract gap kind, which is a different thing: a gap is what an agent reports about something it could not see. ADR-0041.

A VACUOUS PARAMETRIZED TEST IS ONE THAT PASSES AFTER IT STOPS WORKING. No module is labelled `Maturity: deferred`, so the check that a deferred module names a register entry cannot currently fail. The fix is not to skip it: the checking logic is a named function, a second test calls it on a synthetic docstring and requires a failure, and a third asserts the current fact (no module is deferred) so the vacuity is itself measured. Reusable shape for any 'no instance of X exists yet' invariant.

TWO OF THE FIVE SOURCE RECORDS WERE NOT WRITTEN FROM A FETCHED ARTIFACT, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. `sslbl-ja3` is registered in `SOURCES` from `concept/05`, which reports the publisher's own statement about a list static since 2021 — nothing here has ever fetched it. VirusTotal has never been called and its quota is deliberately unspent. A record written from a page is not worthless, it is UNVERIFIED, and every record in `docs/sources/` opens by saying which it is, enforced by test.

THE FULL SUITE IS NOW 2 137 TESTS IN ~895 s (was 1 894 in ~965 s at task 54). Budget a session against fifteen minutes and run it in the foreground. The Bash tool caps at 600 s, so background it and block on the task output inside the same turn — never end the turn expecting to be woken up.
failed_approaches: RUNNING A SECOND `uv run pytest` WHILE THE FULL SUITE WAS RUNNING. I ran `pytest tests/test_governance.py` twice for a quick re-check while the full suite was in flight, and that suite came back with one failure: `tests/test_durability.py::test_the_restored_schema_holds_the_rows_the_backup_came_from`, `['helena_signal_host_context'] did not come back, and none of them reads the clock`. It did not reproduce — the module passed 26/26 alone and the full suite re-run alone was green, 2137 passed — so the most likely cause is CPU contention perturbing the engine's catch-up during the module-scoped drill fixture, which reads `contents(source_engine)` immediately after `run_pipeline` returns. `prds/CONTEXT.md` §4 says one engine per machine and one workspace at a time; that rule covers a second pytest process on the same machine too, and I did not read it that way. Do not do it, and if you see this failure, the lead is that `before` may be read while a materialized view is still behind, not that the backup lost a row.

Writing a sixth new record for each of the six questions that already had one. Started, then abandoned before anything was written: see invariant_conflicts. The closure map is what the task actually needed — a way from a question to its answer — and a duplicate record is a second thing to keep in sync.

Asserting hazard and deferral coverage by searching the register for prose from the notes. The first draft of `test_every_hazard_the_note_records_has_a_section` looked for each hazard's STATEMENT in `docs/hazards.md`, which passes on a paraphrase and fails on a rewrap. It now parses the hazard NAMES out of `concept/08`'s table with a regex and compares them to the register's `## N. <name>` headings as sets, in both directions — an added row fails, a removed row fails, a reworded statement does not. Same shape for the deferral bullets, except one bullet carries four capabilities, so that one needs an explicit phrase-to-keys table (NOTE_DEFERRALS) plus a test that the note has no bullet the table does not cover.
next_session_should_know: Governance is written down and executable; nothing about the pipeline changed. FIVE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE MAP IS `docs/decisions/README.md`. Before treating anything in `concept/08`'s blocking section as open, look there — eleven of twelve are closed and the map names the record. The one that is open is the silently lost record, and it is an accepted hazard (`docs/hazards.md` §2), not a task. (2) THE NEXT RECORD NUMBER IS 0047, and identifiers are never reused — `test_the_record_numbers_are_contiguous_and_never_reused` enforces contiguity, so a record cannot be skipped or renumbered quietly. A new record must also be in the index or `test_every_record_is_in_the_index` fails. (3) IF YOU ADD A SOURCE: a `SourceDescriptor` in `helena.enrichment.SOURCES` without a `docs/sources/<source_id>.md` fails `test_every_registered_source_has_a_record`, and that record must OPEN with either `**Written from a fetched artifact` or `**NOT written from a fetched artifact` — the test asserts exactly one of the two in the first 600 characters. Adding a source is still an escalation. (4) IF YOU DEFER SOMETHING: add an entry to `docs/deferred.md` with a `Key: `slug`` line and a `Re-entry test` line (both parsed), and if a module carries `Maturity: deferred`, its docstring must name that key. `concept/01`'s bar is the one the register holds you to: an experiment or a measured need, not a gap in a diagram. (5) THE FULL SUITE IS 2 137 TESTS IN ~895 s AND MUST BE RUN ALONE. One pytest process at a time on this machine, not just one workspace — running a second one concurrently produced a durability failure that did not reproduce, and failed_approaches has the diagnosis lead in case it recurs on its own.
